questions.question: Education was transferred from state List to concurrent List by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, often referred to as the **Mini-Constitution**, brought about the most extensive changes to the Indian Constitution during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• One of the significant changes was the transfer of five subjects from the **State List** (List II) to the **Concurrent List** (List III) of the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• These five subjects were **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice** (excluding the Supreme Court and High Courts).
 
• By moving **Education** to the **Concurrent List**, the amendment enabled both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** to enact laws on the subject, though central legislation takes precedence in case of a conflict under **Article 254**.
 
• This shift was intended to ensure a **uniform national standard** and policy for education across all states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **44th Amendment Act, 1978**:

 
 
• Passed by the **Janata Government** to nullify several distortions introduced by the 42nd Amendment.
 
• It is most notable for removing the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights and making it a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**.
 
• It inserted the **Tenth Schedule** to prevent political defections by members of Parliament and State Legislatures.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**:
 
 
• Focused on the implementation of the **Right to Education**.
 
• It inserted **Article 21A**, making free and compulsory education for children between **6 and 14 years** a **Fundamental Right**.
 
• It also added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents or guardians to provide educational opportunities.

questions.question: Which Finance Commission was the first to recommend Goods and Services Tax compensation to states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13th Finance Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **13th Finance Commission**, which was chaired by **Dr. Vijay Kelkar** and covered the award period from **2010 to 2015**, was the first to explicitly recommend a compensation package for states to facilitate the rollout of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**.
 
• The commission proposed a **GST Compensation Fund** with an initial corpus of **50,000 crore rupees** to provide a financial cushion for states that might experience revenue shortfalls during the transition to the new indirect tax regime.
 
• It introduced the concept of a **Grand Bargain**, emphasizing that the central government should provide fiscal incentives to states to encourage the adoption of a comprehensive and uniform **GST model** across the country.
 
• The commission argued that while GST would eventually increase the tax base and improve **economic efficiency** by creating a **common national market**, the immediate loss of state-level taxes like **VAT** and **Entry Tax** required a formal compensation mechanism.
 
• These recommendations laid the essential groundwork for the fiscal architecture that was later adopted under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**, which eventually brought GST into effect on **1st July 2017**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **12th Finance Commission**:

 
 
• Chaired by **Dr. C. Rangarajan** (2005–2010), this commission primarily focused on **fiscal consolidation** and incentivizing states to implement the **Value Added Tax (VAT)** system.
 
 
 
• **14th Finance Commission**:
 
 
• Led by **Y.V. Reddy** (2015–2020), it is significant for increasing the vertical devolution of central taxes to states from **32 percent to 42 percent**, providing greater fiscal autonomy to state governments.
 
 
 
• **15th Finance Commission**:
 
 
• Chaired by **N.K. Singh** (2021–2026), it addressed the post-GST fiscal landscape and maintained the devolution share at **41 percent**, accounting for the new status of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Mandate**:
 
 
• The Finance Commission is a **Constitutional Body** established under **Article 280** of the Constitution of India to recommend the distribution of tax proceeds between the **Union and the States**.

questions.question: Mulk Raj Anand's novel Two Leaves and a Bud is based on the exploitation of workers in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tea plantations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Two Leaves and a Bud** is a seminal novel written by **Mulk Raj Anand**, first published in **1937**. It serves as a scathing critique of the **British colonial administration** and the **capitalist exploitation** inherent in the plantation economy.
 
• The narrative is set in the **Macpherson Tea Estate** located in **Assam**, India. The title of the novel is a direct reference to the method of plucking the top **two leaves and a bud** from the tea plant, which yields the highest quality tea.
 
• The story revolves around the protagonist, **Gangu**, a displaced **Punjabi peasant** who is lured to the tea gardens by the false promise of a better life and high wages, only to find himself trapped in a system of **indentured labor** and debt bondage.
 
• Anand vividly depicts the **dehumanizing conditions** faced by the workers, including poor sanitation, physical abuse, and the lack of basic legal rights, highlighting the stark contrast between the laborers' misery and the **hedonistic lifestyle** of the British managers like **Reggie Hunt**.
 
• The novel concludes tragically with the murder of **Gangu** by **Reggie Hunt**, followed by a trial that results in the acquittal of the British officer, thereby illustrating the systematic **injustice** and **racial bias** of the colonial legal system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulk Raj Anand (1905–2004):**

 
 
• He was a prominent **Indian writer** in English and a pioneer of the **Indo-Anglian novel**, alongside R.K. Narayan and Raja Rao.
 
• Anand was a founding member of the **Progressive Writers' Association** and was deeply influenced by **Marxist ideology** and **social realism**.
 
• His other notable works include **Untouchable (1935)**, which explores the life of a sweeper named **Bakha**, and **Coolie (1936)**, which depicts the struggles of a young hill boy named **Munoo** across various urban labor settings.
 
• He was honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in 1971 and the **Padma Bhushan** in 1967 for his contributions to literature and education.

questions.question: Which of the following reports is associated with Human Development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Report**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Report (HDR)** is an annual publication released by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** to measure and analyze global progress in human welfare.
 
• It was first introduced in **1990** by the visionary Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** with the goal of shifting the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
• The report is primarily known for the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, a composite statistic that ranks countries based on three key dimensions: **Long and healthy life** (measured by life expectancy at birth), **Knowledge** (measured by mean and expected years of schooling), and **A decent standard of living** (measured by **Gross National Income (GNI)** per capita).
 
• Unlike traditional economic reports that focus solely on **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, the **HDR** explores critical themes such as poverty, gender inequality, and sustainability to provide a holistic view of human capability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Risks Report**:

 
 
• This is an annual study published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** ahead of its annual meeting in **Davos**.
 
• It identifies and assesses the most significant threats the world faces, categorized into environmental, societal, geopolitical, and technological risks.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Outlook (WEO)**:
 
 
• Published by the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, this report provides a detailed analysis of the global economy and forecasts future growth trends.
 
• It is released twice a year, typically in **April** and **October**, and serves as a vital resource for global policy coordination.
 
 
 
• **Global Competitiveness Report**:
 
 
• Another flagship publication of the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, it measures the **Global Competitiveness Index (GCI)**.
 
• It evaluates factors like institutional quality, infrastructure, and market efficiency to determine the level of productivity of various nations.

questions.question: The Global Energy Transition Index is published by:

options.text: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Economic Forum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Energy Transition Index (ETI)** is a specialized framework designed to track and benchmark the progress of various nations toward a **secure, sustainable, and affordable** energy future.
 
• It is published annually by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, typically in collaboration with **Accenture**, providing a data-driven analysis for policymakers and business leaders.
 
• The index evaluates countries across two primary dimensions: **Energy System Performance** (current state of the energy system) and **Transition Readiness** (the robustness of the enabling environment for future transitions).
 
• The **System Performance** pillar focuses on three core imperatives: **Environmental Sustainability**, **Energy Security and Access**, and **Economic Development and Growth**.
 
• The **Transition Readiness** dimension measures factors such as **Capital and Investment**, **Regulation and Political Commitment**, **Institutions and Governance**, and **Infrastructure**.
 
• In recent editions, such as the **Energy Transition Index 2024**, advanced economies like **Sweden**, **Denmark**, and **Finland** have consistently ranked at the top of the list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF)**

 
 
• Established in **January 1971** by **Klaus Schwab**, it is a non-profit foundation headquartered in **Cologny, Switzerland**.
 
• It is globally recognized for its annual meeting in **Davos**, where political and business elites gather to discuss pressing global issues.
 
• Other prominent reports released by the **WEF** include the **Global Gender Gap Report**, **Global Risks Report**, and the **Global Competitiveness Report**.
 
 
 
• **International Energy Agency (IEA)**
 
 
• An intergovernmental organization established in **1974** in the wake of the **1973 oil crisis**, based in **Paris, France**.
 
• It publishes the flagship **World Energy Outlook** report, which provides comprehensive projections and analysis of global energy trends.
 
 
 
• **World Bank**
 
 
• Headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, it was founded in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference**.
 
• It consists of the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)** and the **International Development Association (IDA)**, primarily publishing the **World Development Report**.
 
 
 
• **OPEC**
 
 
• The **Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries** was founded in **1960** in **Baghdad** and is currently headquartered in **Vienna, Austria**.
 
• Its mission is to coordinate the petroleum policies of its member countries to ensure the stabilization of oil markets.

questions.question: What is the official time duration of a standard FIFA football match (excluding extra/injury time)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**90 min**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Law 7** of the **Laws of the Game** established by the **International Football Association Board (IFAB)** and recognized by **FIFA**, a standard professional football match consists of **two equal periods** of **45 minutes**.
 
• The total official duration of the match, excluding any additional time added for injuries or substitutions, is **90 minutes**.
 
• The **referee** is the sole timekeeper on the pitch and has the authority to signal the end of each **45-minute** half, though they usually add **allowance for time lost** (stoppage time) at their discretion.
 
• Between the two halves, players are entitled to a **half-time interval**, which must not exceed **15 minutes** as per standard regulations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Extra Time**

 
 
• In **knockout competitions** where a winner must be decided, if the match is a draw after **90 minutes**, two extra periods of **15 minutes** each are played, totaling **120 minutes**.
 
 
 
• **Stoppage Time**
 
 
• This is the time added at the end of each half to compensate for **substitutions**, **player injuries**, **disciplinary sanctions**, or **VAR reviews**.
 
 
 
• **Shortened Matches**
 
 
• While **90 minutes** is the standard for senior football, certain **youth**, **senior (veteran)**, or **disability football** matches may be played over **80 minutes** (two 40-minute halves) or shorter durations depending on competition rules.

questions.question: The Life Insurance Corporation of India was nationalized to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mobilize savings for planned development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)** was established on **September 1, 1956**, after the Parliament passed the **Life Insurance Corporation Act** earlier that year.
 
• The primary motive behind nationalization was to **mobilize small savings** from the public and channel them into **long-term investments** required for the **Second Five-Year Plan** and subsequent **planned economic development** of the country.
 
• Nationalization aimed to spread **life insurance** more widely, particularly in **rural areas**, ensuring that the benefits of financial security reached the socially and economically backward classes.
 
• The government sought to protect **policyholders** from the mismanagement, frequent failures, and unethical practices of the **private insurance companies** that dominated the market prior to 1956.
 
• By consolidating the industry, the state gained control over substantial **investible funds**, which were utilized for **nation-building** activities, infrastructure projects, and the development of the **public sector**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Historical Background of LIC:
 
 
• The **Government of India** issued an ordinance on **January 19, 1956**, taking over the management of insurance businesses before full nationalization.
 
• LIC was formed by the amalgamation and nationalization of **245 Indian and foreign insurers** and provident societies.
 
• The **Finance Minister** at the time of nationalization was **C.D. Deshmukh**, who envisioned the corporation as a tool for **social welfare** and capital formation.
 
• The official motto of LIC is **Yogakshemam Vahamyaham**, which is derived from the **Bhagavad Gita** and translates to 'Your welfare is my responsibility'.
 
• Currently, **LIC** is one of the largest **institutional investors** in India, significantly contributing to the **equity and debt markets**.

questions.question:
Shankardeva's teachings are primarily based on which sacred texts?

I. Bhagavad Gita

II. Bhagavata Purana
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement I: The **Bhagavad Gita** is a cornerstone of **Shankardeva’s** teachings, particularly the concept of **Eka Sarana**, which emphasizes total surrender to **Lord Krishna** as the supreme deity. Hence, statement I is correct.
 
• Statement II: The **Bhagavata Purana** serves as the primary theological and philosophical source for his **Neo-Vaishnavite movement**; he translated its core sections into **Assamese** to make them accessible to the masses. Hence, statement II is correct.
 
• The religious system established by **Shankardeva** is known as **Eka Sarana Nama Dharma**, which focuses on the worship of one God through the chanting of His name (**Nama**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Srimanta Shankardeva** (1449–1568):

 
 
• A great 15th-century polymath and saint-reformer from **Assam** who propagated **Vaishnavism**.
 
• He introduced the **Sattriya dance**, which is now recognized as one of the **eight classical dances** of India.
 
• He founded the **Satras** (monasteries) and **Namghars** (community prayer halls) that continue to be centers of cultural and religious life in **Assam**.
 
• His literary works include the **Kirtan Ghosha**, a collection of poetical verses meant for community singing, and the **Borgeets**, which are classical devotional songs.
 
• He advocated for an egalitarian society, rejecting **caste-based discrimination** and complex **sacrificial rituals** in favor of simple **Bhakti** (devotion).

questions.question: Which of the following scheme is related to Residential Education for Students?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SHRESHTA Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SHRESHTA** (Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas) was launched by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** to provide high-quality education to meritorious **Scheduled Caste (SC)** students.
 
• The primary objective is to enhance the reach of development interventions and to bridge the educational gap for **SC students** by providing them entry into high-quality **private residential schools**.
 
• Admissions are targeted for **Class 9** and **Class 11**, focusing on students whose parental annual income does not exceed **2.5 lakh rupees**.
 
• Selection is performed through a transparent mechanism called the **National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS)**, which is conducted by the **National Testing Agency (NTA)**.
 
• The scheme is implemented in two modes: one involving direct admission to **CBSE-affiliated private schools** and another involving support to **NGO-run residential schools** and hostels for primary and secondary education.
 
• It covers the complete expenditure for the student, including **school fees** and **hostel charges**, ensuring that socio-economic background does not hinder the academic growth of bright students.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UDAN Scheme**:

 
 
• Known as **Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik**, it is a regional airport development and **Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)** of the **Ministry of Civil Aviation**.
 
• It aims to make air travel affordable and widespread, stimulating **inclusive economic growth** and infrastructure development in underserved regions of India.
 
 
 
• **PM-KUSUM**:
 
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan** was launched by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**.
 
• It focuses on **solarizing agriculture** by providing subsidies for **solar pumps** and establishing grid-connected solar power plants on barren lands.
 
 
 
• **FAME India Scheme**:
 
 
• Standing for **Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles**, it is part of the **National Electric Mobility Mission Plan**.
 
• It promotes the manufacturing of **electric and hybrid vehicle** technology and provides incentives to consumers to reduce the dependency on fossil fuels and lower **vehicular emissions**.

questions.question: The term 'Upanishads' literally means _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sitting down beside**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **Upanishad** is derived from the **Sanskrit** language, composed of the roots **Upa** (near), **Ni** (down), and **Sad** (to sit).
 
• Literally, the term means **sitting down beside** or near a teacher to receive instructions on the most profound **spiritual truths** and **philosophical concepts**.
 
• The name reflects the **Guru-Shishya** (teacher-disciple) tradition of ancient India, where students sat at the feet of a master to learn **esoteric knowledge** that was not intended for the general public.
 
• These texts represent the **Jnana Kanda** (knowledge section) of the **Vedas**, focusing on the nature of existence rather than ritualistic ceremonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Philosophy of Upanishads:**

 
 
• They are frequently referred to as **Vedanta**, meaning the **end of the Vedas**, signifying the highest goal of Vedic knowledge.
 
• The central theme involves the relationship between **Atman** (the individual soul) and **Brahman** (the universal reality).
 
• Major concepts like **Samsara** (cycle of birth and death), **Karma** (actions), and **Moksha** (liberation) find their primary development in these texts.
 
 
 
• **Important Upanishads:**
 
 
• There are **108 Upanishads** recognized in the **Muktika** canon, though 10 to 13 are considered **Mukhya** (principal) Upanishads.
 
• The **Brihadaranyaka Upanishad** is one of the oldest and contains the famous prayer **Asato ma sadgamaya**.
 
• The **Mundaka Upanishad** is the source of the Indian national motto, **Satyameva Jayate**.
 
• The **Chandogya Upanishad** is noted for the phrase **Tat Tvam Asi** (That Thou Art).

questions.question: 'Majuli festival' is celebrated in which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Majuli Festival** is an annual cultural celebration held in **Majuli**, the largest river island in the world, situated in the **Brahmaputra River** in the state of **Assam**.
 
• The festival typically takes place in the month of **November**, aiming to showcase the rich cultural heritage and traditional diversity of the indigenous communities living on the island.
 
• It provides a significant platform for the promotion of **Sattriya**, which is one of the eight major **Indian Classical Dances**, originated by the 15th-century saint and reformer **Srimanta Sankardev**.
 
• During the event, various ethnic groups like the **Mishing**, **Deori**, and **Sonowal Kacharis** exhibit their traditional music, dance forms, and unique culinary delicacies.
 
• The festival also highlights the **Neo-Vaishnavite** culture through exhibitions of local handlooms, bamboo crafts, and pottery, reflecting the socio-religious history of the **Sattras** (monasteries).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goa**

 
 
• Famous for the **Goa Carnival**, a vibrant celebration characterized by parades, floats, and music reflecting **Indo-Portuguese** culture.
 
• Celebrates **Shigmo**, a spring festival involving traditional folk dances like **Ghode Modni** and **Fugdi**.
 
 
 
• **Kerala**
 
 
• Renowned for **Onam**, a harvest festival featuring the **Vallam Kali** (snake boat race) and **Pookalam** (floral carpets).
 
• Celebrates **Vishu**, the astronomical New Year, and **Thrissur Pooram**, famous for its grand display of caparisoned elephants.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**
 
 
• Home to the **Mysuru Dasara**, a state festival celebrating the victory of Goddess **Chamundeshwari**.
 
• Known for **Kambala**, an annual buffalo race held in the coastal regions of the state.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of combustion? I. Rapid combustion II. Spontaneous combustion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rapid combustion** is a process in which a substance burns rapidly and produces a large amount of **heat** and **light** in a very short duration. This occurs when an external source like a spark or a flame is provided, such as the burning of **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)** in a kitchen stove or a matchstick catching fire. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Spontaneous combustion** refers to a type of combustion that occurs without the application of any external heat or spark. The substance catches fire on its own when its **ignition temperature** is reached through internal heating or atmospheric conditions. Notable examples include the spontaneous burning of **white phosphorus** at room temperature and devastating fires in **coal mines** caused by coal dust. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other classifications of combustion processes include:
 
 
• **Explosion**: This is a sudden combustion reaction that results in the evolution of heat, light, and a large volume of **gas** accompanied by **sound**. It is commonly observed during the ignition of **firecrackers**.
 
• **Complete Combustion**: Occurs in the presence of **sufficient oxygen**, producing **carbon dioxide** and water. It is characterized by a **non-luminous blue flame**.
 
• **Incomplete Combustion**: Takes place when the **oxygen supply is limited**, leading to the formation of **carbon monoxide**, carbon soot, and water. It is typically identified by a **yellow luminous flame**.
 
• **Ignition Temperature**: The minimum temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its **ignition temperature**; a substance cannot catch fire as long as its temperature is lower than this value.

questions.question: Hindustan Socialist Republican Army (HSRA) was founded in a meeting held at which of the following places?

options.text: Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** was established in **September 1928** during a historic meeting held at the **Ferozeshah Kotla ground** in **Delhi**.
 
• The organization was a transformation of the **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)**, which had been founded in **October 1924** in **Kanpur** by **Sachindra Nath Sanyal** and **Ram Prasad Bismil**.
 
• The leadership of the **HSRA** included prominent revolutionaries such as **Chandrashekhar Azad**, **Bhagat Singh**, **Sukhdev Thapar**, and **Bhagwati Charan Vohra**.
 
• The inclusion of the word **'Socialist'** in the name was a result of the influence of **Marxist** ideologies, aiming for a revolution that would end all forms of exploitation.
 
• The primary goal of the **HSRA** was to establish a **Federal Republic of the United States of India** through an armed revolution against the **British Raj**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay**:

 
 
• This venue hosted the **first session** of the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in **December 1885**.
 
• The session was presided over by **Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee** and organized by **A.O. Hume**.
 
 
 
• **Alfred Park in Allahabad**:
 
 
• This location is where **Chandrashekhar Azad** fought his final battle against the **British police** on **February 27, 1931**.
 
• Azad shot himself with his last remaining bullet to uphold his vow of never being captured alive.
 
 
 
• **Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar**:
 
 
• Site of the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** on **April 13, 1919**, where **General Dyer** ordered troops to fire on a peaceful crowd.
 
• This event was a major catalyst for the **Non-Cooperation Movement** and led **Rabindranath Tagore** to renounce his **knighthood**.

questions.question: In the context of Indian Budget, which of the following is included in the revenue expenditure?

options.text: Expenditure on acquisition of combat aircraft
Expenditure on acquisition of naval ship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subsidies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure** consists of all those expenditures of the government which do not result in the creation of physical or financial **assets**. It relates to those expenses that do not reduce the **liabilities** of the government and are typically recurring in nature.
 
• **Subsidies** are a primary component of revenue expenditure in the **Indian Budget**. They are transfer payments made by the government to producers or consumers (such as **Food Subsidies**, **Fertilizer Subsidies**, and **Petroleum Subsidies**) to ensure the affordability of essential goods. These payments are consumed within the fiscal year and provide no direct asset return.
 
• The **Union Budget** classifies expenditures into revenue and capital. Revenue expenditure is essential for the day-to-day running of government machinery and the delivery of **social welfare** services. In recent years, subsidies have accounted for roughly **7% to 9%** of the total revenue expenditure of the **Government of India**.
 
• In contrast, expenditures on **Combat Aircraft**, **Naval Ships**, and **Expressway construction** are classified as **Capital Expenditure** because they involve the acquisition of long-term assets or infrastructure that enhance the nation's productive or defensive capacity over many years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Expenditure (CapEx)**:

 
 
• **Defense Acquisition**: The procurement of high-value hardware like **fighter jets** and **warships** is recorded under the **Capital Outlay on Defense Services**.
 
• **Infrastructure Development**: The construction of **Expressways** and **National Highways** creates tangible public assets, stimulating long-term economic growth.
 
• **Asset Creation**: Any expenditure that leads to the creation of **machinery**, **equipment**, or **buildings** is categorized here.
 
 
 
• **Other Revenue Expenditure Components**:
 
 
• **Interest Payments**: This is usually the largest single item of revenue expenditure, representing the cost of servicing the **Public Debt**.
 
• **Salaries and Pensions**: Payments made to government employees and retired personnel are mandatory revenue outlays.
 
• **Grants-in-aid**: Grants provided to **State Governments** and **Union Territories** are technically revenue expenditures, even if they are utilized for creating capital assets at the state level.

questions.question: The QUAD leader's summit-2025 will be held in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QUAD)** is a strategic diplomatic partnership consisting of four nations: **India**, the **United States**, **Australia**, and **Japan**.
 
• During the **2024 QUAD Leaders' Summit** held in **Wilmington, Delaware**, it was officially announced that **India** would host the next summit in **2025**.
 
• Initially, **India** was slated to host the summit in **2024**; however, following a mutual agreement and a request from the **U.S. President**, the hosting sequence was swapped, resulting in the **USA** hosting in 2024 and **India** taking the lead for **2025**.
 
• The **2025 Summit** in India will focus on advancing the **Indo-Pacific** agenda, including maritime security, **critical technologies**, climate action, and health security.
 
• This hosting duty underscores **India's** growing role in the **Indo-Pacific region** and its commitment to a rules-based international order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of QUAD**:

 
 
• The concept was first proposed by Japanese Prime Minister **Shinzo Abe** in **2007** but gained significant momentum when it was revived in **2017**.
 
• The first-ever **In-Person Leaders' Summit** took place in **September 2021** at the **White House**, Washington D.C.
 
 
 
• **Previous Summit Locations**:
 
 
• **Japan**: Hosted the summit in **Tokyo** in **2022** and coordinated a meeting on the sidelines of the **G7 Summit** in **Hiroshima** in **2023**.
 
• **Australia**: Originally scheduled to host the **2023** summit in **Sydney**, though the venue was shifted to Japan due to domestic political scheduling in the **USA**.
 
• **USA**: Hosted the **2024** summit in the hometown of President **Joe Biden**, emphasizing personal diplomacy.
 
 
 
• **Core Initiatives**:
 
 
• The group promotes the **IPMDA (Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness)** to track dark shipping and illegal fishing.
 
• Other pillars include the **Quad Vaccine Partnership** and the **Quad Fellowship** for STEM students.
